---
title: "Top-k Sampling"
description: "A decoding method that samples the next token from only the k highest-scoring candidates."
term: "Top-k Sampling"
letter: "T"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Top-k sampling limits a model's next-token choices to the $k$ most likely
tokens, then samples among those choices. It removes the long tail of
low-scoring alternatives for each generation step.

## Technical explanation

Given next-token logits, top-k decoding retains the $k$ largest logits,
masks the rest, normalizes the remaining scores, and samples from the
result. The candidate set changes at each step. Top-k is commonly combined
with temperature and other decoding controls.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Top-k offers a direct bound on the number of candidate tokens considered
during sampling and can reduce unlikely continuations. A fixed $k$ may be
too restrictive when the model's distribution is flat and too permissive
when it is sharply peaked.

## How it works

At each generation step, the decoder selects the $k$ highest-scoring
tokens, sets other logits to negative infinity, applies any temperature
scaling, and samples from the normalized distribution over the remaining
candidates.

## Practical example

A creative writing application can compare several top-k values on a fixed
prompt set and evaluate diversity, coherence, and repetition. Keep the
model, prompts, and other decoding settings fixed to understand the effect
of changing $k$.

## Common misconceptions

- Top-k limits candidate count, not the number of tokens in the final
  response.
- A larger $k$ does not always improve quality; it permits more low-ranked
  candidates to be sampled.
